name: Joe Biden
description: US president whose administration expanded infrastructure investment, industrial policy and climate spending.
scope: Public positions and conduct during the specified period; this represents the individual rather than all party members or citizens.

axes.brief: Competitive elections and constitutional accountability were defended during his presidency.
axes.counter: Executive orders and a familial pardon complicate a maximal accountability reading.

axes.brief: Gun regulation and health measures coexisted with protest and constitutional speech protections.
axes.counter: Drug policy and national-security secrecy did not uniformly follow liberty claims.

axes.brief: Diversity and minority inclusion accompanied a shared American civic identity.
axes.counter: Recognition of diversity does not mean cultural expectations always override common law.

axes.brief: Legalisation and family pathways coexisted with removal and tighter 2024 asylum controls.
axes.counter: Early reform proposals differed from late-term border restrictions.

axes.brief: Alliance defence and aid to Ukraine and Israel coexisted with Afghanistan withdrawal.
axes.counter: Avoiding direct war with Russia qualifies military resolve; past Senate votes are outside scope.

axes.brief: NATO and Paris cooperation were strengthened while national currency and border authority remained.
axes.counter: US resistance to comprehensive international criminal jurisdiction limits supranationalism.

axes.brief: Private enterprise and providers operated alongside public infrastructure and subsidised services.
axes.counter: Industrial subsidies and public funding do not by themselves establish public ownership.

axes.brief: Buy American procurement and retained or raised tariffs accompanied allied trade cooperation.
axes.counter: Selective protection differs from comprehensive import exclusion.

axes.brief: Private production coexisted with CHIPS investment, wage support and sectoral industrial policy.
axes.counter: Industrial strategy did not create compulsory production targets for most businesses.

axes.brief: Expanded child tax credits and progressive tax proposals supported income redistribution.
axes.counter: Temporary benefits and legislative defeat limit claims of permanent universal expansion.

axes.brief: Civil institutions and reproductive law were defended independently of Biden’s Catholic belief.
axes.counter: Religious ceremonies and exemptions persisted without clerical legislative vetoes.

axes.brief: Marriage recognition, LGBT inclusion and reproductive choice were supported in this presidency.
axes.counter: Earlier DOMA and abortion positions are not silently projected into the scoped period.

axes.brief: Infrastructure, clean energy and AI adoption coexisted with safety and reliability safeguards.
axes.counter: A pro-investment policy is not approval of uncertain embryo or brain enhancement.

axes.brief: Federal civil-rights standards and national programmes coexisted with constitutional state powers.
axes.counter: States retained constitutions, police and taxation; unilateral secession was not endorsed.

reasons.4: The scoped national institutions retained constitutional states with their own governmental constitutions. Federal programme supremacy does not remove that protected institutional role.
reasons.5: State and local police retained ordinary jurisdiction. National security coordination does not establish support for replacing them with a single national police authority.

axes.brief: His explanations of racial disparities emphasised discrimination and unequal opportunity.
axes.counter: Modern neurobiology comparisons are not established by these explanations.
axes.gap: Specific claims about IQ, temperament and inherited behaviour remain provisional; anti-discrimination policy is contextual evidence rather than a scientific causal position.
